'''Thomas Earl Robinson''' (born March 17, 1991) is a [[college basketball]] player for the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]].

==High School==
Robinson played high school basketball at [[Brewster_Academy|Brewster Academy]] in [[washington, New_Hampshire|Wolfeboro, NH]]. Robinson averaged 16 points, 13 rebounds and 5 blocks per game his senior year.

Robinson was rated the No. 24 recruit by Scout.com, No. 31 by Rivals.com and No. 40 ESPNU 100 as a high school senior. <ref>[http://www.kuathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/robinson_thomas00.html]</ref>

==College career==
As a freshman Robinson played in 33 games with one start and averaged 7.2 minutes, 2.5 [[points per game|points]] and 2.7 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] per game. As a sophomore he played in 33 games with two starts and averaged 14.6 minutes, 7.6 points and 6.4 rebounds per game.

Robinson began his junior year and the 2011-2012 Men's College Basketball season as one of the 50 candidates for the preseason [[John R. Wooden Award]].<ref>[http://www.woodenaward.com/?p=1105 John R. Wooden Award Announces Men's Preseason Top 50 List]</ref> Along with senior teammate [[Tyshawn Taylor]] Robinson was expected to become one of the leaders for the Kansas team. On December 31, 2011 in a game against the [[University of North Dakota basketball|University of North Dakota,]] Robinson scored 30 points and grabbed 21 rebounds. He was the first Kansas player to achieve 30/20 since [[Wayne Hightower]] scored 36 points and grabbed 21 rebounds in a 1961 game against the [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|University of Missouri]].<ref>[http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=313652305]</ref>. At the end of the Big 12 conference regular season, Robinson was second in the nation with 22 [[double-double|double doubles]] behind O.D. Anosike of [[Siena Saints men's basketball|Siena College]]. At that point, Robinson averaged 18 points and 11.9 rebounds.

Prior to their game on January 22, 2011 against [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]], Kansas players, coaches and fans held a moment of silence honor of Robinson, who had lost his grandmother, his grandfather, and his mother all within three weeks of each other. After the game Kansas coach [[Bill Self]] said "For him to even be out there on the court was remarkable."<ref>{{cite news |title=Thomas Robinson's mother dies |url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/news/story?id=6048355 |publisher=[[ESPN.com]] |date=January 22, 2011 |accessdate=2012-03-06}}</ref>

On March 4, 2012, Robinson was named the [[Big 12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|2012 Big 12 Player of the Year]]. All-Big 12 awards are selected by the league’s head coaches.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/kan/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/2011-12/misc_non_event/12allbig12.pdf|title=2012 Phillips 66 All-Big 12 Men's Basketball Awards Announced|author=Big 12 Conference |publisher=''Big 12 Conference'' |accessdate=March 4, 2011}}</ref>  On March 5, 2012, he was named the Associated Press Big 12 Player of the Year.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2012/basketball/ncaa/wires/03/05/2060.ap.bkc.all.big.12.team.1st.ld.writethru.0957|title=Kansas' Robinson is AP Big 12 player of year|author=Associated Press |publisher=''Sports Illustrated'' |accessdate=March 5, 2012}}</ref>

On April 9, 2012 Robinson decided to forgo his senior season and declare for the [[2012 NBA Draft]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Kansas' Thomas Robinson to turn pro|url=http://espn.go.com/nba/draft2012/story/_/id/7792384/kansas-jayhawks-thomas-robinson-forgo-senior-year-enter-nba-draft|work=ESPN.com}}</ref>
